title: Petro Government Suspends Arrest and Extradition Warrants for 29 Clan del Golfo Leaders
detail: Colombia's Peace Commissioner signed a resolution suspending arrest and extradition warrants for 29 Clan del Golfo (Autodefensas Gaitanistas de Colombia / EGC) leaders, including top commander alias 'Chiquito Malo', as a negotiation incentive under President Petro's Total Peace policy. The move immediately triggered a public institutional crisis: the Attorney General's Office refused to comply, keeping the warrants active in defiance of the executive. Critics and opposition lawmakers condemned the measure as an unprecedented capitulation to a designated criminal organization, while the government argued dialogue was the only path to reducing drug-trafficking violence.

title: Analysis: Petro's Last-Minute Constituent Assembly Bid Described as Constitutionally 'Impossible'
detail: Legal and political analysts published assessments concluding that President Petro's push to convene a constituent assembly before his term expires in August 2026 is constitutionally unworkable. Petro launched signature-collection committees on Labor Day (May 1) targeting 2.5–5 million signatures to modify the 1991 Constitution, framing it as a final legacy effort. Legal scholars noted the timeline — with presidential elections scheduled for May 31 — makes any assembly convocation during the current term legally and logistically impossible. The move is widely viewed as a political message rather than a viable constitutional project.

media.caption: Analysis of Petro's constituent assembly push
